sources.title: Former Nvidia CEO Huang agreed to testify at public US Senate hearing, senator's aide says
COP31 climate summit risks failure as talks go deep into overtime

stories.topic: UNITED STATES / NVIDIA / JENSEN HUANG / AI / GOVERNANCE / EXPORT COMPLIANCE
stories.headline: Former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang agrees to public Senate testimony; date unconfirmed
stories.body: Reuters reported on 20 November that an aide to Senator Tim Scott said former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang agreed to testify at a public US Senate hearing. Lawmakers are examining China-related allegations and questions concerning advanced AI-chip exports. Scott's office did not confirm a hearing date; its original request named 3 December. A separate closed-door interview with three House committees was planned for 1 December. Huang's spokesperson declined comment. Agreement to testify is not a finding of misconduct, and the public hearing date remains unconfirmed. No directly attributable Nvidia share-price or earnings impact was verified.
stories.analysis: Testimony may clarify governance and export-compliance questions; allegations, committee findings and measured financial effects remain distinct.
stories.watch_next: Confirmed public hearing date, the separate House interview, official testimony and company disclosures.

stories.topic: COP31 / TURKEY / EUROPEAN UNION / CLIMATE / ENERGY TRANSITION / CLIMATE FINANCE
stories.headline: COP31 negotiations run into overtime with fossil-fuel and climate-finance divisions unresolved
stories.body: Reuters reported on 21 November that negotiators from nearly 200 countries remained divided at COP31 in Antalya, Turkey, after the scheduled Friday conclusion. Disputes concerned fossil-fuel transition language and support for poorer countries adapting to climate change. Thursday's draft removed earlier fossil-fuel references and a proposed US$120bn adaptation-finance target. EU climate commissioner Wopke Hoekstra warned that no agreement remained possible. This describes a negotiating draft and unresolved talks, not an adopted agreement, a realised funding cut or a confirmed final summit failure. No directly attributable oil-price, carbon-market, bond-yield or FX move was verified.
stories.analysis: Unresolved climate finance and energy-transition provisions create longer-term policy uncertainty; their investment implications depend on the eventual agreed text and implementation.
stories.watch_next: Final negotiating text, any confirmed agreement, adaptation-finance provisions and fossil-fuel language.
